newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU revised proposals seek compulsory beef labelling.
newsitem.headline: EU revised proposals seek compulsory beef labelling.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday presented revised proposals, making beef labelling and stricter cattle identification measures compulsory in all EU member states by January, 1, 2000, a spokesman said.
Countries could introduce the measures earlier if they wished, the spokesman added.
The proposals were revised following objections from the European Parliament, which last month was given joint decision-making powers in this area.

The new proposals, which are intended to help restore consumer confidence after the public health scare over bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), will be discussed by EU farm ministers at their next meeting on March 17-18.
The proposals will then be sent to the European Parliament for scrutiny.
EU member states last week criticised the decision to give the parliament an effective right to veto the proposals, saying this could result in a substantial delay in the urgent legislation.
Further details of the revised proposals were not immediately available.
